title: ESA CCI Soil Moisture COMBINED Product (v09.2, daily 0.25°)
description: The ESA Climate Change Initiative Soil Moisture COMBINED product merges Level-2 surface soil moisture retrievals from active (scatterometer) and passive (radiometer) microwave satellites — from SMMR and SSM/I through AMSR-E, ASCAT, SMOS, SMAP, AMSR2, GPM and FengYun-3 — into a single daily climate data record of volumetric surface soil moisture (m3 m-3) on a 0.25° global grid, with per-pixel uncertainty and quality flags, from November 1978 to December 2024 (v09.2).
purpose: The longest consistent satellite record of surface soil moisture, suitable for agricultural-drought climatologies and anomaly analysis over northern Algeria and for evaluating models (ERA5-Land, GLEAM) and the shorter SMAP record.

spatial_extent.description: Global 0.25° grid (CEDA: longitude −180 to 180, latitude −90 to 90); Algeria must be subset. Retrievals are missing or flagged where sensors cannot retrieve soil moisture (e.g. frozen or snow-covered soil, dense vegetation).

temporal_extent.description: v09.2 covers 1978-11-01 to 2024-12-31 and is a temporal extension of v09.1. Newer CCI versions are released periodically; the C3S service (DOI 10.24381/cds.d7782f18) extends the same algorithm close to real time (updated three times a month).

format: NetCDF-4 classic (one global file per day)

variables.name: flag
variables.description: Quality flags: snow/temperature below zero, dense vegetation, no convergence, value outside physical bounds, weight below threshold, all datasets unreliable, barren-ground advisory

variables.name: sensor
variables.description: Contributing sensors (SMMR, SSMI, TMI, AMSRE, WindSat, AMSR2, SMOS, AMIWS, ASCAT A/B/C, SMAP, GPM, FY3B/C/D, MODEL)

processing: Level-2 soil moisture from scatterometers (ERS AMI-WS, Metop ASCAT) and from radiometers retrieved with the LPRM algorithm are quality controlled, rescaled to a common climatology, merged using weights based on error estimates (triple collocation), and homogenised for structural breaks at sensor transitions (Gruber et al. 2019; Preimesberger et al. 2021). The 'sensor' and 'freqbandID' flags list 'MODEL' among their meanings.
validation: Validation and product-quality assessment are documented by the CCI Soil Moisture project (product validation and user documents linked from the ESA CCI catalogue page); no single accuracy figure is given on the CEDA record.
limitations: Represents only the top few centimetres of soil; root-zone moisture is not provided in this product.
Coarse 0.25° cells (about 28 km) mix irrigated plains, rainfed cereals, rangeland and bare soil in northern Algeria.
The flag variable includes a 'barren_ground_advisory_flag', relevant to large parts of the Algerian Sahara; such pixels should be screened before use.
Spatial and temporal coverage are uneven before the 2000s (fewer sensors, gaps between overpasses); merged series contain sensor-transition effects despite homogenisation.
Version v09.2 ends in December 2024; for recent months use the C3S near-real-time product (note its known issue: 1–20 September 2026 values in v202505 should not be used, per a CDS warning).

algeria_notes: Most informative over the Tell and High Plateaux cereal belt, where rainfed soil-moisture anomalies drive yields. Over the Sahara, screen pixels with the barren-ground advisory and other flags. Irrigated perimeters and oases are much smaller than a 0.25° cell and are not resolved. For agricultural drought indicators combine with root-zone estimates (GLEAM, ERA5-Land) rather than using surface moisture alone.
